application_guidance.input_pattern: Exact SANP updates with a known finite initial divergence and a compatible norm/strong-convexity normalization.
read_original_when: Using the printed Theorem 4.1 coefficient instead of Eq. (4.22).
Seeking convergence part (b), Theorem 4.2 rates, boundary iterates, inexact prox updates or stochastic variants.
sensitive_conditions: The steps and dual norms use the same geometry as σ.
All required gradients and exact updates are defined; interior preservation is explicitly assumed here.
The output metric is a minimum of historical values, not the final iterate.
The source coefficient discrepancy must remain visible.

complexity_scope.guarantee: Deterministic finite-horizon inequality for all allowed choices under the stated assumptions.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: No hidden multiplicative constants: the explicit coefficient is 1/(2σ); geometry enters through B and the dual norms.
complexity_scope.oracle: One chosen exact subgradient per update and an exact Bregman subproblem solver. Value access is additional if a minimizing historical index must be returned.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Minimum objective gap among x1,…,xK. The statement does not guarantee the last-iterate gap. A realizing output is x_j for any j minimizing these K objective values.
complexity_scope.regime: Arbitrary finite K≥1 and positive steps; finite B and finite subgradients. No Theorem 4.2 anytime rate or accuracy-based oracle budget is inferred.
complexity_scope.resource: A run performing K updates uses K subgradient calls and K exact prox solves; optional best-iterate selection needs up to K separate value queries and K−1 comparisons. No universal arithmetic or prox-solver runtime is supplied.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Only the specified exact SANP trajectory with well-defined interior iterates; no lower bound or coverage of all first-order algorithms.

content.intended_use: Control a finite-horizon SANP objective gap through initial Bregman divergence and weighted squared subgradient norms.

proofs.full_local_argument: Fix K and all objects in the statement. Write d_s=x_s−x_{s+1} and B_s=Bψ(x*,x_s). Since x_{s+1} is an exact minimizer of the convex differentiable prox objective on convex X, for every x∈X its feasible directional derivative gives <t_s g_s+∇ψ(x_{s+1})−∇ψ(x_s),x−x_{s+1}>≥0. This remains applicable when x=x* is a boundary point because the derivative is evaluated at interior x_{s+1}; the segment to x* is feasible. Consequently t_s<g_s,x_{s+1}−x*>≤<∇ψ(x_s)−∇ψ(x_{s+1}),x_{s+1}−x*>. The three-point identity, with a=x_{s+1}, b=x_s, c=x*, rewrites the right side as B_s−B_{s+1}−Bψ(x_{s+1},x_s). By the subgradient inequality, t_s(f(x_s)−f*)≤t_s<g_s,x_s−x*>=t_s<g_s,d_s>+t_s<g_s,x_{s+1}−x*>. The dual-norm inequality and (sqrt(σ)||d_s||−t_s||g_s||*/sqrt(σ))²≥0 imply t_s<g_s,d_s>≤(σ/2)||d_s||²+(t_s²/(2σ))||g_s||*². Strong convexity gives Bψ(x_{s+1},x_s)≥(σ/2)||d_s||². Combining these facts proves t_s(f(x_s)−f*)≤B_s−B_{s+1}+(t_s²/(2σ))||g_s||*². Sum s=1,…,K: Σ t_s(f(x_s)−f*)≤B_1−B_{K+1}+(1/(2σ))Σ t_s²||g_s||*². Strong convexity also gives B_{K+1}≥0, including a boundary comparator x*. Finally positivity of the t_s gives (Σ t_s)min_{1≤s≤K}(f(x_s)−f*)≤Σ t_s(f(x_s)−f*). Drop the nonpositive term −B_{K+1} and divide by Σ t_s>0 to obtain the conclusion. All terms are finite by the assumptions. No rate tuning, convergence limit, boundary-gradient extension or unproved transfer is used.
proofs.locator: Source proof: printed pp.171–172 / PDF pp.5–6, (4.16)–(4.22). The following complete argument is a local reconstruction, separate from source text.
map: Exact prox optimality gives the comparison inequality.
Apply the three-point identity and the subgradient inequality.
Apply dual-norm Young inequality and cancel the strong-convexity term.
Telescope and compare the weighted average with the minimum.
proofs.omitted_details: None for the selected finite-horizon inequality. Other source results are not part of this proof.

source_discrepancies.detail: (4.15) prints 2σ^{-1}; (4.21)–(4.22) print (2σ)^{-1}. This record selects the latter and verifies it by the complete local argument.

assumptions: X is closed and convex with nonempty interior. f is convex and L_f-Lipschitz on X for the fixed norm, for a finite L_f≥0. Its minimum is attained and a subgradient is computable, as in Assumption A.
ψ:X→R is finite-valued, σ-strongly convex for this same norm with σ>0, and continuously differentiable on int X. The normalization is Bψ(u,v)≥(σ/2)||u−v||² for u∈X and v∈int X.
x1∈int X. Each stated exact update attains its minimum and x1,…,x_{K+1} belong to int X. This is an explicit selected regime of the source well-definedness assumption.
Each g_s is a finite subgradient satisfying f(x)≥f(x_s)+<g_s,x−x_s> for all x∈X. Each t_s>0. The comparator x* may lie on the boundary of X; B is finite.
statement.conclusion: min_{1≤s≤K}[f(x_s)−f*] ≤ [Bψ(x*,x1)+(1/(2σ))Σ_{s=1}^K t_s²||g_s||*²]/[Σ_{s=1}^K t_s]. This is the coefficient in source Eq. (4.22), not a verbatim transcription of Eq. (4.15).
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let n≥1, fix a norm ||·|| on R^n and its dual ||z||*=max_{||v||≤1}<v,z>. Let X⊂R^n and f:X→R satisfy the assumptions below; f*=min_X f and x*∈argmin_X f. Define Bψ(u,v)=ψ(u)−ψ(v)−<∇ψ(v),u−v>. Let x_{s+1}=argmin_{x∈X}{t_s<g_s,x>+Bψ(x,x_s)} with g_s∈∂f(x_s). Write B=Bψ(x*,x1).
statement.parameter_domains: n,K positive integers; σ>0; 0≤L_f<∞; t_s∈(0,∞). No compactness assumption and no predetermined bound on B are required for this finite-horizon inequality.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every integer K≥1, every positive sequence t1,…,tK, every permitted sequence of subgradient choices and exact updates satisfying these assumptions, and every x*∈argmin_X f. The claim is deterministic and contains no expectation.
